root_cause.text: In `svc_rdma_copy_inline_range`, the `memcpy` destination offset incorrectly used the page index (`rc_curpage`) instead of the byte offset within the page (`rc_pageoff`), causing out-of-bounds writes to arbitrary memory.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `memcpy(dst + head->rc_curpage, ...)` to `memcpy((unsigned char *)dst + head->rc_pageoff, ...)`, and the CVE description explains that `rc_curpage` (a page index) was mistakenly used as a byte offset.

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In `svc_rdma_copy_inline_range`, the `memcpy` destination offset incorrectly used the page index (`rc_curpage`) instead of the byte offset within the page (`rc_pageoff`), causing out-of-bounds writes to arbitrary memory.
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `memcpy(dst + head->rc_curpage, ...)` to `memcpy((unsigned char *)dst + head->rc_pageoff, ...)`, and the CVE description explains that `rc_curpage` (a page index) was mistakenly used as a byte offset.

candidates.rationale: Increments the page count used as index for the page array; though not directly vulnerable, it contributes to the page indexing that leads to the wrong offset usage.
Obtains the base address of the current page but does not incorporate the correct byte offset; the subsequent memcpy uses this base with an incorrect offset.
Core vulnerability: uses head->rc_curpage as the byte offset instead of head->rc_pageoff, causing out-of-bounds writes beyond the intended page region.
Updates the total bytes read counter; part of the inline copy state machine, though not directly responsible for the memory corruption.
Updates the byte offset within the page; this variable was intended to be used in memcpy but was mistakenly replaced by rc_curpage, highlighting the root cause discrepancy.

vuln_statements.explanation: Core vulnerability: uses head->rc_curpage (page index) as the byte offset instead of head->rc_pageoff, causing out-of-bounds writes beyond the intended page region.
Obtains the base address of the current page using rc_curpage as index; the subsequent memcpy then incorrectly uses the same rc_curpage as a byte offset, contributing to the vulnerability.
Updates the correct byte offset within the page (rc_pageoff), but this variable was mistakenly not used in the memcpy destination offset, highlighting the root cause discrepancy.
Increments the page count used as index for the page array; contributes to the page indexing mechanism that, combined with the offset error, leads to out-of-bounds writes.
Updates the total bytes read counter; part of the inline copy state machine, not directly responsible for the memory corruption but part of the incorrect offset propagation.
